candidates.attacker_control: The attacker fully controls the bytes of an OpenWire frame: the command type byte selects the ExceptionResponse marshaller and the following tight/loose encoding carries the class name string and the message string that become createThrowable's arguments. No credentials or prior handshake are required because unmarshal occurs while reading the command, before TransportConnection/authentication processes it. The same code is also reachable in the reverse direction, so a malicious broker can attack connecting clients' JVMs.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Class.forName is called with initialize=false, so static initializers alone are not triggered by loading the class. The return is cast to Throwable, which throws for non-Throwable classes — but construction (and its side effects) already happened before the cast, and the catch(Throwable) swallows it. No allowlist exists on this path, in contrast to ObjectMessage handling in ClassLoadingAwareObjectInputStream.checkSecurity, which enforces org.apache.activemq.SERIALIZABLE_PACKAGES; this contrast shows the missing validation is not an intentional trust-all design for OpenWire. Exploitability depends on classpath contents in a given deployment; the default distribution includes Spring. No runtime test was executed, so this is a source-level lead, not a confirmed exploit.
candidates.impact: Unauthenticated remote code execution capability in the JVM of the broker (and symmetrically of any client that connects to a malicious broker) when a suitable class is on the classpath; at minimum it grants arbitrary class instantiation with an attacker-supplied string argument, which for classes like Spring's XML application-context loaders means loading and executing attacker-controlled configuration. All OpenWire versions share the flaw, so downgrading the negotiated wire format does not remove it.
candidates.prerequisites: Network reachability to an OpenWire connector (the shipped conf/activemq.xml exposes openwire on tcp://0.0.0.0:61616 with no authentication plugin enabled by default). A class with a public single-String constructor whose construction has security-relevant side effects must exist on the target's classpath — the default binary distribution ships Spring, so a class such as org.springframework.context.support.ClassPathXmlApplicationContext is a representative reachable gadget. No privileges beyond a TCP connection are needed.
candidates.root_cause: BaseDataStreamMarshaller.createThrowable (v12 and all other OpenWire versions) takes the className and message straight from the wire, does Class.forName(className) and constructor.newInstance(message) without verifying Throwable.class.isAssignableFrom(clazz) and without any package allowlist. The (Throwable) cast only fails after the constructor has already executed, and the resulting Throwable/ClassCastException is swallowed by the catch block, so the side effect of the attacker-chosen constructor is the only observable behavior. The same createThrowable implementation exists in v1/v9/v10/v11/v12 marshallers and in activemq-openwire-legacy v2.
candidates.title: OpenWire ExceptionResponse unmarshalling instantiates an attacker-named class with an attacker-controlled String argument (pre-auth RCE class)
candidates.trace: TcpTransport.doRun (line 232) -> readCommand (239-241) -> OpenWireFormat.unmarshal/doUnmarshal (354-373, chooses tight or loose unmarshal from the wire) -> ExceptionResponseMarshaller.tightUnmarshal (65-71) or looseUnmarshal (109-115) -> BaseDataStreamMarshaller.tightUnmarsalThrowable (187-192) or looseUnmarsalThrowable (508-513), each of which reads clazz=String, message=String from the DataInput -> createThrowable (227-235) -> Class.forName(className, false, ...) -> clazz.getConstructor(String.class) -> constructor.newInstance(message). Because newInstance runs before the Throwable cast, a non-Throwable class with a side-effecting String constructor is executed and the later ClassCastException is caught, returning a placeholder Throwable.
candidates.unverified: Whether a concrete side-effecting String-constructor gadget is present in every deployment (default distribution ships Spring, but custom deployments may lack usable classes). Exact exploit behavior and post-exploitation impact were not executed or verified at runtime; no payload is provided.
candidates.weakness_type: Deserialization of untrusted data / unsafe reflection (CWE-502, CWE-470)

coverage_summary: Snapshotted repository is Apache ActiveMQ 5.15.8 (pom 5.15.8, SCM tag activemq-5.15.8), 2688 model-visible files; per get_source_scope no sensitive-name/path, symlink, or >5MiB exclusions (binary-like files are unreadable/skipped, which applied to a small number of matches). I inspected the client transport/OpenWire marshalling layer, broker transports and default assembly configuration (conf/activemq.xml, conf/jetty.xml, conf/jetty-realm.properties, webapps/api WEB-INF/web.xml, webapps/admin web.xml), JAAS LDAP login module, activemq-web servlets/renderers, activemq-web-console JSPs, JMS ObjectMessage/ClassLoadingAwareObjectInputStream, STOMP XStream support, JDBC store SQL construction, LevelDB FileSupport, and searched for command execution, script engines, XXE-prone parsers, URL/SSRF sinks, and servlet parameter use. I did not read all 2688 files exhaustively and did not execute code, tests, or scanners.
limitations: Static, source-only review: no runtime confirmation, exploitability proof, or scanner output; the candidate is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.

Exploitability of the OpenWire path depends on a usable class (public String constructor with side effects) being present on the target classpath; only the default distribution contents (which include Spring) were considered.
Dependency-level vulnerabilities (e.g., bundled Spring, XStream, Commons BeanUtils, Jetty versions) were not enumerated or assessed.

The snapshot is a released tag, so it contains several distinct historical weaknesses (LDAP empty-password bind, web-console XSS, Jolokia exposure); the one-candidate cap forced selecting only the strongest, and the rejected leads were not exhaustively traced.

Tests and non-Java resources (except configuration/JSPs relevant to security) were not deeply reviewed; large generated marshaller copies across OpenWire versions were sampled rather than read in full.

rejected_leads.lead: LDAPLoginModule authentication bypass: login() converts a null password to "" (lines 125-128) and bindUser() binds with empty credentials (401-420), which LDAP servers may treat as an unauthenticated/anonymous bind and accept, authenticating the user without a password.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires LDAP-backed JAAS auth to be configured and the LDAP server to permit unauthenticated binds; environment-dependent and lower impact than the pre-auth OpenWire path. Genuine weakness worth noting, but not selected as the single candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Stored/reflected XSS in the web console: javascript: hrefs built from message destinations/IDs in message.jsp (lines 154, 168) and other JSP output paths.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires an authenticated console session plus admin interaction; message.jsp generally uses c:out escaping. Impact and certainty lower than the OpenWire candidate; not fully traced across all JSPs.

rejected_leads.lead: Jolokia JMX bridge deployed at /api/jolokia (assembly/src/release/webapps/api/WEB-INF/web.xml) with BASIC auth roles user,admin and default admin/admin credentials in conf/jetty-realm.properties, and no jolokia-access.xml restricting MBean exec operations.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires valid web-console credentials (default admin/admin is itself a deployment weakness); configuration/credential-dependent rather than a pure source flaw in this snapshot.
Mitigated in-source: resolveClass/resolveProxyClass call checkSecurity and enforce the org.apache.activemq.SERIALIZABLE_PACKAGES allowlist by default; not an unguarded vulnerability in this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: QueueBrowseServlet mass property assignment: all request parameters are pushed into IntrospectionSupport.setProperties on a renderer resolved from the untrusted 'view' parameter (activemq-web QueueBrowseServlet.java lines 93-120).
rejected_leads.reason: The instantiated type is limited to classes registered under META-INF/services/org/apache/activemq/web/view/, so arbitrary class loading was not demonstrated; renderer setters are simple (contentType, maxMessages). Unconfirmed and lower impact.

rejected_leads.lead: STOMP/XStream message transformation allowlist includes broad packages (java.util, org.apache.activemq) via XStreamSupport.createXStream.
rejected_leads.reason: Uses XStream's permission system with an explicit allowlist rather than unrestricted types; no concrete gadget chain identified in this snapshot.

summary: Reviewed the Apache ActiveMQ 5.15.8 source snapshot (activemq-parent 5.15.8, SCM tag activemq-5.15.8; 2688 files, all modules). I traced the OpenWire unmarshalling path from the TCP transport through OpenWireFormat into the generated data-stream marshallers and found that ExceptionResponse/Throwable fields are unmarshalled by reading a class name and a message string off the wire, loading the named class with Class.forName and invoking its public single-String constructor — with no check that the class is actually a Throwable. This is the one issue with clear attacker-controlled input crossing the network trust boundary into a sensitive reflective instantiation; it is duplicated in every OpenWire marshaller version (v1–v12 and the legacy v2 module). No candidate met the bar better; the other plausible leads (LDAP empty-password bind, web-console XSS, Jolokia/JMX exposure, ObjectMessage deserialization) are either configuration-dependent, mitigated in-source, or weaker in impact and are recorded as rejected leads. No runtime confirmation was performed; all conclusions are from static source reading.
